Summary: A Greek physician and philosopher who practised in Rome in the 2nd century and wrote extensively on medicine, logic, and philosophy.
KeyPoints: Galen mentions Christians alongside Jews as people who follow doctrines without demonstration; He praises their moral discipline, self-control, and willingness to face death for their convictions, comparing them to philosophers; The brief remarks confirm a distinct, disciplined Christian community known to an educated Roman observer in the 2nd century
